name: RT-2 VLA Study Note
observations: Purpose: study note comparing the RT-2 paper (Brohan et al., 2023, arXiv:2307.15818v1) with current best-practice tooling for vision-language robotics. Created 2026-11-01 from local PDF pdf/embodied_ai_papers/RT-2, Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control, Anthony Brohan et al., 2023, v1_compressed.pdf (26 pages), plus Context7 docs lookup for LeRobot v0.6.1.

Core RT-2 idea: a vision-language-action (VLA) model is a pretrained vision-language model co-fine-tuned to emit robot actions directly, with NO new parameters or action-only layers -- the model weights are shared across language and action tasks.

Action-as-text recipe: the 8-D action vector is 'terminate, dpos_x, dpos_y, dpos_z, drot_x, drot_y, drot_z, gripper_extension' (6-DoF end-effector delta + gripper + episode-termination flag). Each continuous dimension is discretized into 256 uniform bins, so an action becomes 8 integers, e.g. '1 128 91 241 5 101 127'.

Token mapping: PaLI-X provides a unique token per integer up to 1000, so bins map directly to integer tokens; PaLM-E has no such scheme, so the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten to form the action vocabulary -- a form of symbol tuning.

Training format: inputs are the robot camera image plus a standard VQA prompt, 'Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A:', and the target is the string of action tokens. This reuses the VLM's native text interface instead of a bespoke action head.

Co-fine-tuning is the key recipe: mix the original web-scale vision-language data (VQA, captioning, interleaved image-text) with robot trajectories, upweighting the robot dataset's sampling weight in each batch. Robot-only fine-tuning generalizes measurably worse because the model forgets web concepts.

Output constraint: when prompted with a robot-action task, decoding is restricted to valid action tokens; on standard VLM tasks the model may still emit the full natural-language vocabulary. This keeps actions executable without sacrificing language ability.

Backbones and instantiations: RT-2-PaLI-X built from PaLI-X at 5B and 55B parameters; RT-2-PaLM-E built from 12B PaLM-E. Robot data came from the RT-1 protocol (13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen, language-annotated trajectories).

Real-time inference pattern: 55B models cannot run on robot GPUs, so RT-2 is served from a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network, letting one service drive multiple robots. Achieved 1-3 Hz for the 55B model and ~5 Hz for the 5B model.

Evidence: ~6,000 real-world evaluation trials with a 7-DoF mobile manipulator. On generalization to unseen objects/backgrounds/environments RT-2 is ~2x better than RT-1 and MOO and ~6x better than pretrained-representation baselines (VC-1, R3M); on emergent-skill suites it reaches >3x the best baseline.

Emergent capabilities transferred from web pretraining: symbol understanding ('move apple to 3', 'push coke can on top of heart'), visual/math/multilingual reasoning ('move the apple to cup with same color', 'move X near the sum of two plus one', 'mueve la manzana al vaso verde'), and human recognition ('move the coke can to the person with glasses').

Ablations: training a large VLM from scratch performs very poorly; co-fine-tuning beats robot-only fine-tuning at every size; larger models generalize better. PaLM-E variant was stronger on math reasoning and hard generalization, PaLI-X stronger on symbol understanding.

Chain-of-thought variant: a PaLM-E-based RT-2 was fine-tuned for a few hundred gradient steps on data augmented with a 'Plan:' sentence before the action tokens ('Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: 1 128 124 136 121 158 111 255.'). This bridges VQA and manipulation data and yields multi-stage semantic reasoning, e.g. a rock as an improvised hammer or an energy drink for a tired person.

Simulation result: a smaller PaLI-3B co-fine-tuned model on the open Language-Table environment with 2-D delta actions encoded as 'X Y' in [-10..10] scored 90 +/- 10 versus LAVA 77 +/- 4, RT-1 74 +/- 13, BC-Zero 72 +/- 3, at ~5 Hz.

Stated limitations: web pretraining transfers semantics and visual concepts but not new physical skills -- motions stay bounded by the robot-data distribution; inference cost is high and becomes a bottleneck for high-frequency control (authors point to quantization/distillation); few openly fine-tunable VLMs existed at the time (they cite LLaVA as a hope).

name: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models
observations: Model class that maps (camera observation, language instruction) directly to low-level robot actions inside a single end-to-end network, while retaining web-scale vision-language pretraining.

Differs from two-stage LLM-planner pipelines: in a VLA the same weights do high-level semantic reasoning and low-level closed-loop control, rather than a state machine handing primitives to separate controllers.
Practical benefits over prior VLM-for-robotics designs (CLIPort, MOO): no restricted 2-D action space, no calibrated camera requirement, and no action-only model layers.

name: RT-2 (Robotics Transformer 2)
observations: Brohan et al., 2023, Google DeepMind; arXiv:2307.15818v1; project site robotics-transformer2.github.io.
Introduces vision-language-action models by co-fine-tuning PaLI-X (5B/55B) and PaLM-E (12B) to output text-tokenized robot actions.
Shows emergent semantic reasoning, symbol understanding, multilingual instruction following, and chain-of-thought planning for manipulation.

name: LeRobot
observations: Hugging Face LeRobot (/huggingface/lerobot), docs version v0.6.1, 4500+ code snippets, high source reputation -- the de facto open-source stack for end-to-end robot learning and VLA workflows.

Training is CLI-driven: `lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true --dataset.repo_id=lerobot/libero --env.type=libero --steps=100000 --batch_size=64`. Supports VLA families (smolvla, pi0, pi0_fast) alongside act and diffusion policies, and can push checkpoints to the Hub via --policy.push_to_hub.

Parameter-efficient adaptation matches RT-2's 'avoid catastrophic forgetting' concern: LoRA fine-tuning via `--peft.method_type=LORA --peft.r=64 --peft.lora_alpha=64` with a ~10x higher learning rate (1e-3) than full fine-tuning.

Async inference mirrors RT-2's cloud-served policy pattern: `python -m lerobot.async_inference.policy_server --host/--port` runs the policy server (gRPC), and `python -m lerobot.async_inference.robot_client` on the robot supplies observations. Key tuning knobs: actions_per_chunk (action chunking) and chunk_size_threshold, with aggregate_fn_name=weighted_average over overlapping chunks.

Real-Time Chunking addresses the 1-5 Hz latency problem RT-2 reports: `lerobot-rollout --inference.type=rtc --inference.rtc.execution_horizon=10 --inference.rtc.max_guidance_weight=10.0` gives smooth continuous motion for large slow VLA models (pi0, pi0.5, SmolVLA).

Simulation benchmarks for safe iteration: LIBERO, LIBERO-plus, and VLABench environments integrate directly with lerobot-train for periodic evaluation (--env_eval_freq) and episode-level success metrics.

Recommended pairing: Hugging Face Transformers for the VLM backbone (e.g. PaliGemma-class models), Hugging Face Hub/Datasets for LeRobotDataset storage and sharing, LeRobot for policy training/serving, and PyTorch as the runtime.

name: Action Tokenization as Text
observations: Reuse a VLM's existing tokenizer as the action codec, so no architecture change is needed to go from captioning to acting.
256 uniform bins per continuous dimension is enough for closed-loop manipulation when the policy runs at 1-5 Hz and re-plans every step.
Requires reserving/overwriting a block of vocabulary tokens and constraining decoding to them during robot-task prompts.
Modern alternatives implement the same idea with faster decoding (e.g. pi0_fast / FAST-style tokenization in LeRobot) to raise control frequency.
